title: MongoDB Atlas Pricing: Plans, Costs & Savings (2026)
summary: MongoDB Atlas pricing ranges from free to $30/month on Flex, then to hourly rates on dedicated, so you can plan the transition before scaling.
body_markdown:
## Frequently asked questions


### Is MongoDB Atlas free for production use?


No: the free M0 tier is documented as a place to learn and prototype. Its limits on storage, throughput and connections make it unsuitable for an app with paying users.


If you remember the old shared M2 and M5 tiers, Flex is MongoDB's replacement, and it meters usage up to a ceiling. If the app earns money, price Flex or a dedicated cluster, and treat M0 as a staging environment.


### Can Atlas be paused to stop being billed?


Only partly, and only on dedicated clusters. Pausing stops the hourly compute charge, but the docs say **storage and backup costs for a paused cluster** keep accruing, and Atlas resumes a paused cluster automatically after a limited period.


For a staging cluster you use a few days a month, pausing suits. It doesn't suit a production database you want to stop paying for. For that, export the data and terminate the cluster.


### Does Atlas charge for data you read out of it?


Atlas meters data leaving the cluster, not the reads themselves. Traffic into Atlas is free, while traffic out to the internet or across regions or cloud providers is billed per gigabyte. A chatty API in the same region as the database costs little here.


When a reporting job runs in another region, or a service returns large documents to browsers, it shows up as a transfer line on the invoice.


Private networking options add their own cloud-provider charges on top. See the data transfer section of the Atlas billing documentation for the current rates.


### Is MongoDB Atlas cheaper through the AWS Marketplace?


Not on list price. Buying through the AWS Marketplace consolidates the Atlas charge onto your AWS invoice and can count toward an existing AWS spending commitment, which has real value if you already hold one.


At the per-hour and per-gigabyte level, the rates are the same as buying direct. Any lower price comes from a private offer, and that means a sales conversation. Ask for the written rate card before you assume a discount.


### How do I set a spending limit on Atlas?


**Atlas has no hard cap that stops a dedicated cluster from billing once it passes a dollar amount.** You approximate one with controls. In the billing settings, create alerts on organization spend so a surprise reaches you mid-month instead of on the invoice.


On each cluster, set the maximum tier for compute auto-scaling and decide deliberately whether storage auto-scaling stays on. Flex is the exception, since its metered billing stops at a ceiling. That's the reason to start a small app there.
